title: Have we entered a new age of AI-enabled scientific discovery?
body: Mathematicians, computer scientists and other researchers have made breakthroughs in their work using AI agents, such as the one available through OpenAI’s ChatGPT. AI agents actively break down your initial question into a series of steps and may search the web to complete a task or provide an in-depth answer. At drug companies, researchers are developing systems that combine agents with other AI-based tools to discover new medicines. Engineers are using similar systems to discover new [...] Other scientists are using AI as a buddy, too. In October 2025, mathematician Ernest Ryu of UCLA shared a new proof that he discovered with the help of ChatGPT running on GPT-5 pro. The proof has to do with a branch of math and computer science called optimization, which focuses on finding the best solution to a problem from a set of options. Some methods for doing this jump around, unable to settle on a single solution. Ryu (and the AI model) proved that one popular method always converges on [...] At the first scientific meeting for research led by AI agents in October, human conference attendees noted that the AI often made mistakes. One team published a paper about their experience, detailing why agents based on LLMs are not ready to be scientists.

And AI is proving particularly useful in finding treatments for rare diseases that are often overlooked by pharmaceutical companies, due to the lack of financial incentive afforded by so few potential patients. [...] Researchers at McGill University in Montreal, Quebec, Canada, recently used AI to repurpose drugs for Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF), a rare, progressive lung disease characterised by the scarring and thickening of lung tissue. Their approach involved modelling the progression of the disease with an AI model.

My belief is, in the next five to 10 years, the majority of new drug development could be guided by AI – Jun Ding [...] Collins and his team trained a generative AI model to recognise the chemical structures of known antibiotics. This allowed the algorithm to learn what it takes to kill bacteria. The researchers then used the AI to screen more than 45 million different chemical structures00855-4) for their ability to target _Neisseria gonorrhoeae_, the bacteria that cause gonorrhoea, and _Staphylococcus aureus,_ a significant source of infections in the form of MRSA.

title: AI-powered cyberattacks outpace security patches, expert warns | The Jerusalem Post
body:
"This is a trend that's actually common around AI usage," the executive stated. "Attackers are building more sophisticated infrastructure to conduct complex cybersecurity campaigns at scale, and AI is no longer an assistant – it's actually the operator behind at least some of those operations."

### Human error remains a major security vulnerability [...] "Just like we have defense in depth that tries to secure every part of the organization, attackers are always going to target the weakest link, whether it's human or not," he said.

The scale of attacks targeting employees is also growing rapidly, Zanger warned.

He cited a 500% surge in the use of "ClickFix," a technique in which attackers impersonate IT administrators and trick employees into taking actions that compromise their organization's systems. [...] Major corporate breaches are also increasingly relying on coordinated social engineering tactics rather than purely technical attacks, Zanger noted.

He pointed to the massive Binance hack, which he said did not begin with a brute-force attack on the company's systems. Instead, attackers conducted fake job interviews that tricked employees into downloading malware.

title: DFRobot’s DX-M1 Is An AI Accelerator That Uses Your M.2 Slot And Brings 25 TOPS Of Performance At 5W For Just $139, But Forget About Running Heavy LLMs
body:
Power hungry GPUs and expensive cloud API subscriptions are the standard when dabbling with LLMs, but edge computing requires a completely different approach. Most users do not require massive server racks just to handle localized computer vision or object detection tasks, and that’s where hardware like DFRobot’s DX-M1 comes into play. Requiring just one M.2 slot on your motherboard, this AI accelerator packs some serious inference muscle into a standard storage input while costing only $139. [...] Despite packaging the same footprint as the newest PCIe NVMe Gen 5 SSD, this AI accelerator module pushes out a respectable 25 TOPS of INT8 compute while pulling a measly 2W to 5W of power. In short, you won’t even feel that electricity bill when you’re busy deploying continuous, localized AI workloads on mobile robotics or compact setups without dealing with noisy cooling assemblies or severe thermal throttling. [...] ##### Related Story The Cheapest AM5 X3D Build Starts At $649 With Ryzen 7 7700X3D, B650 Motherboard And 32 GB DDR5 RAM Kit Dropping From $954 To Just $649

Underneath the hood, the hardware is configured to operate entirely independently of your machine’s primary system RAM, thanks to its 4GB of onboard LPDDR5 RAM, which is dedicated to loading neural network weights, alongside 1Tbit (128GB) of QSPI NAND Flash for firmware stability and storing compiled models locally.

title: Going deep on local AI performance benchmarking with Apple’s Mac Studio with M5 Ultra taking on Nvidia DGX Spark — inference engine recipes mandatory for bigger models as MLX stack matures | Tom's Hardware
body:
Apple’s updated Mac Studio with the M5 Ultra SoC has already proven itself as one of the most powerful systems around, thanks to its 36-core CPU and 80-core GPU with Neural Accelerators for the matrix math operations that drive AI compute. Beyond that raw power, options for up to 512GB of unified memory have many local AI enthusiasts lining up for the 13 to 15 weeks it’ll take for Apple to ship one right now. [...] We expect (and can only hope) that improved inference engine support and serving recipes for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 on the M5 Ultra will arrive in time as community members unleash their coding agents on this hardware, because the performance potential is clearly there for Apple Silicon.

### Bottom line [...] Even as Apple closes the performance shortfalls of its hardware for AI inference, development and support around the MLX stack has a ways to go before it catches up with the maturity and performance, as well as the model and inference engine options, available on Nvidia hardware.
